#2195. Como Women, l'australiana Chidiac nominata per il FIFPRO Merit Award 2026

La centrocampista del Como Women e dell’Australia Alex Chidiac è in corsa per il FIFPRO Merit adwars, il premio che viene assegnato al giocatore o alla giocatrice per il proprio impegno sociale e civile. Assieme all’australiana in corsa ci sono anche l’olandese Jeremie Frimpong, il brasiliano Joao Gomes, il congolese Christian Luyindama, il beninese Steva Mounie, il colombiano Walmer Pacheco, lo spagnolo Julio Pleguezelo, la sudcoreana Ji So-Yun, la finlandese Tinja-Riikka Korpela (ex Rona), la svedese Zacira Musovic e la statunitense Phallon Tullis-Joyce.

Importante riconoscimento per Alexandra Chidiac, centrocampista del Como Women, inserita tra le candidate al FIFPRO Merit Award 2026 per il suo impegno sociale e il contributo offerto a iniziative legate alla parità di genere, all’istruzione, alla lotta alla homelessness e alla sostenibilità ambientale.

Attraverso Common Goal e diverse organizzazioni, Chidiac ha sostenuto progetti a favore di donne e ragazze, programmi dedicati alle persone senza fissa dimora e iniziative per sensibilizzare sul ruolo del calcio nella lotta ai cambiamenti climatici. La calciatrice ha inoltre contribuito al fondo per l’impatto sociale della PFA Australia, prendendo posizione anche a tutela dei diritti delle giocatrici.

Tra le esperienze più significative, la partecipazione alla FIFA Series in Kenya, dove ha potuto incontrare le ragazze e lo staff di Moving The Goal Post Kenya, organizzazione no-profit che utilizza il calcio come strumento di emancipazione e crescita per le giovani donne. Un progetto che Chidiac sostiene da otto anni e che ha coinvolto oltre 50.000 donne e ragazze in tutto il Paese.

Istituiti nel 2008, i FIFPRO Merit Awards premiano i calciatori e le calciatrici che, attraverso il proprio impegno, contribuiscono a promuovere il cambiamento nella società. I riconoscimenti sono suddivisi in tre categorie: Player Activism, Player Impact e Player Voice.

Il nome della vincitrice sarà annunciato il 19 novembre 2026, in occasione dell’Assemblea Generale FIFPRO a Panama. A ciascun vincitore sarà inoltre destinata una donazione di 10.000 dollari da parte di FIFPRO a sostegno della propria iniziativa.

Il Como Women si congratula con Alexandra per questo importante riconoscimento e per il valore del suo impegno dentro e fuori dal campo.

#2194. Wolves man sent off and slammed for ‘schoolboy’ performance in UEFA Nations League defeat

Wolves centre-back Ladislav Krejci serves as Czechia’s captain and was called up once again for their latest round of UEFA Nations League fixtures. The 27-year-old was sent off against Spain in his last international outing, and unfortunately, he met the same fate in another fixture against the world champions on Thursday.

Krejci was sent off for dragging down Roberto Fernandez as he broke through on goal, and his side went on to lose 2-0. Somewhat unsurprisingly, the Wanderers man faced strong criticism from the Czech media post-game.

As quoted by Sport.cz, former Czech international and pundit Marek Jankulowski said: “The red card was well-deserved; he misjudged it. The disallowed goal was also a schoolboy mistake, and offside saved us there. Krejčí weakened the team and the chances of equalising decreased.”

The same outlet issued a scathing review in their player ratings, highlighting inaccurate passes and failure to track runs, with Yeremy Pino’s disallowed goal as an example. His red card brought an end to a ‘defensively lacklustre performance’, Sport.cz wrote.

Krejci holds a key role with Czechia as their captain, and he played in the FIFA World Cup over the summer. When fit and available, he nearly always starts for his country and usually plays the full 90 minutes.

However, red cards have cut his last two games short – and against the same opposition. The Wolves man must hate to see Spain fixtures approaching, with both matches ending in defeats as well.

Krejci acknowledged a need to be “careful” about being sent off ahead of the match, but it seems he didn’t heed his own warning. A tough game for the defender was capped off by another red card, and he will be eager to move on and leave it in the past.

This means he will be suspended for Sunday’s game against Croatia. That is the final international fixture of 2026 for Czechia.

It has been another tough international break for Krejci, but he has found better fortunes with Wolves. Following an uncertain summer, he has reclaimed his place in the starting XI and has had a positive impact on form.

The defender has started the last five Championship games, none of which have ended in defeat. Krejci scored in the win over Cardiff City and provided an assist in the late comeback against Bristol City too.

Despite his Thursday night struggles, Krejci will hope to maintain his strong club form when league football returns next week. Wanderers host Charlton Athletic in the Championship on Saturday 21st November, and the Czechia defender will be backed to retain his spot in Cesar Peixoto‘s side.

#2192. Romano: “Varela è nella lista degli obiettivi, il Napoli si è informato e ci sono stati contatti con l’entourage”

Fabrizio Romano, giornalista ed esperto di mercato, sul suo canale Youtube ha fatto il punto sulla trattativa del Napoli per Gustavo Varela, centravanti del Monza: “Giovanni Manna ha da tempo rapporti molto buoni con un’agenzia spagnola importante (Roc Nations, ndr) che rappresenta tra gli altri l’eroe della finale della coppa del Mondo Ferran Torres. Questa agenzia ha in mano diversi giocatori del Napoli. Uno è Rafa Marin, che quest’anno sta facendo molto bene ed è tra i pochi giocatori del Napoli ad avere una valutazione pressoché positiva, essendo tra i rientranti. In questo momento il club azzurro non ha urgenza di rinnovare il suo contratto, ma ha tutta l’intenzione di andare avanti insieme e la questione si rinvierà nel 2027. C’è anche Alisson Santos nella stessa agenzia, ma non si tocca. Per il Napoli non è mai stato in discussione, è un giocatore su cui il club punta. L’incontro con l’agenzia c’è stato, invece, per Gustavo Varela. Un nome da mettere tra il primo, secondo e terzo posto nella lista obiettivi. Questo ragazzo sta facendo cose straordinarie a Monza, complimenti al club brianzolo per averlo preso a 2,5-3 miloni bonus compresi è stato un colpo di genio da parte del direttore Pedro Obiang. Poi c’è il Benfica che ha una clausola di matching rights, dove vanta il diritto di prelazione sul giocatore e può pareggiare le stesse cifre offerte dalle pretendenti. Il Monza dovrebbe fare una chiamata al direttore Mario Branco e il presidente Rui Costa dicendo: “Volete il giocatore e pareggiare l’offerta?”. Se il club lusitano la pareggia sarà poi il giocatore a decidere. Questa è la clausola che vanta il Benfica oltre ad una percentuale sulla vendita. Il Napoli si è mosso, si è informato, ma sulle tracce del giocatore ci sono anche diversi club stranieri dopo questo inizio brillante di stagione. Gli azzurri a gennaio vogliono prendere un attaccante soprattutto se dovesse partire Lucca. Il Napoli è attento sul ragazzo e ci sono stati già diversi contatti con l’entourage”.

#2189. Middlesbrough man urged to stay in January by ex-football chief amid ‘best option’ claim

Middlesbrough could face a battle to keep hold of the attacker down the line amid expected attention from elsewhere. He is under contract until June 2031 after he penned a long-term five year contract in the last transfer window.

Lankshear, 21, joined Boro from Tottenham Hotspur. He has since scored 15 goals in 16 games in all competitions under the guidance of Kim Hellberg.

Brown, who used to work for Manchester United, has delivered his verdict on the forward, as per a report by Football Insider: “Will Lankshear’s best option would be to stay doing what he’s doing with Middlesbrough. He’s showing what he can do in the Championship at the moment, and it’s been key to his development that he’s been willing to drop down into that league to become a regular.”

He added: “If he was to make a move to the Premier League, is that form going to continue? You’d like to think so, but it’s far from certain. It’s a big jump. At the moment, he’s better off sticking with Middlesbrough where he knows he can be successful, helping them achieve their goals, and then seeing what’s next.”

Middlesbrough are unlikely to sell Lankshear this winter, especially halfway through a campaign. He has been linked with an exit to Newcastle United in the Premier League but a departure would be a surprise.

If Boro fail to go up, they will find it hard to retain his services next summer. He is one of the most exciting talents in the EFL right now and has a bright future ahead of him in the game.

He was snapped up by his current club to bolster their attacking department. The England youth international has since established himself as their most prized asset.

Lankshear, who is from Hertfordshire, knows where the back of the net is at second tier level. He is on course to surpass 30 goals at his current rate.

Middlesbrough have been without Lankshear in their last two outings due to injury. He sat out of their 2-0 loss away at Wrexham.

He was also missing in their 0-0 draw at Watford last time out before the international break. Boro seriously miss him when he isn’t playing and they need other players to step up in his absence.

Kyle Joseph joined them from Hull City in July but he has struggled to make an impact and he hasn’t scored in the league yet. David Strelec is another option but he has been injured this term and is still finding his feet again.

Middlesbrough are sat joint-top of the table along with Birmingham City and Stoke City as they look to reach the top flight under Hellberg. They were beaten in the play-off final by Hull City at Wembley back in May and are eager to bounce back with promotion.

#2188. Inter, no alla quinta punta: c'è questa convinzione nel club. Si riflette in difesa. E se parte...

Inter, no alla quinta punta: c'è questa convinzione nel club. Si riflette in difesa. E se parte...

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

In casa Inter sono giorni di riflessioni. Col mercato invernale che si avvicina, i dirigenti nerazzurri studiano come intervenire per migliorare la rosa a disposizione di Cristian Chivu. Nei giorni scorsi si è parlato molto dell'eventualità di inserire una quinta punta in rosa, ma, come riporta il Corriere dello Sport, in casa nerazzurra sono piuttosto convinti di avere a disposizione le risorse necessarie per competere ad alti livelli su tutti i fronti fino al termine dell’annata. "Quella appena attraversata, secondo la dirigenza nerazzurra, è soltanto una curva a gomito della stagione, in cui gli imprevisti si sono beffardamente sovrapposti, costringendo Chivu a spremere più di tutti Marcus Thuram".

"C’è un altro fronte però che effettivamente potrebbe spingere l’Inter a valutare un investimento nel mercato di riparazione. Si tratta della difesa, dove John Stones è già reduce da un lungo infortunio, sulla falsariga di quanto accaduto negli ultimi anni. Le prossime settimane serviranno a capire quali garanzie riuscirà a dare l’ex Manchester City, prima di sondare eventualmente nuovi profili da poter inserire in corso d’opera. Anche perché, al netto delle condizioni di Stones, l’impressione è che manchi qualcosa nella retroguardia nerazzurra in termini di caratteristiche dopo gli addii di De Vrij e Acerbi".

"A livello di liste non ci sono particolari ostacoli da superare, in Serie A come in Champions League, ma va da sé che eventuali cessioni di esuberi possano nel caso agevolare anche operazioni in entrata. In tal senso rimane piena disponibilità da parte dell’Inter ad ascoltare offerte per esempio su Luis Henrique, già tra i possibili partenti in estate".

#2187. Barcellona e Real in ansia per le stelle, Ancelotti: "Salute giocatori priorità del Brasile"

Carlo Ancelotti, allenatore della nazionale di calcio brasiliana, ha assicurato che "i club possono stare tranquilli" perché la sua priorità è "la salute dei giocatori": l'ex allenatore di Milan e Juventus ha risposto in questo modo ai timori espressi da alcuni club europei sull'opportunità che le loro stelle andassero a giocare le amichevoli in Asia, contro Giappone e Singapore. Le sue parole in particolare sembrano una risposta alle preoccupazioni fatte filtrare da Barcellona e Real Madrid per Raphinha e Vinicius.

Queste le parole di Ancelotti: "La priorità è sempre la salute del giocatore. Se è al 100%, si allena. Se è al 100%, gioca. E sotto questo aspetto, controlliamo i minuti che gioca. I club possono stare tranquilli con la nazionale. La priorità per tutti è la salute dell'atleta. Vogliamo sempre che l'atleta torni a giocare e senza infortuni".

L'allenatore ha anche affermato in merito ai tanti giovani convocati: "È un periodo di prova che finirà con questa pausa internazionale della FIFA. La prossima volta definiremo meglio la nostra rosa. È stato un periodo che ci ha fornito molte informazioni sui giovani giocatori. Sappiamo di avere giocatori giovani di grande talento e impegnati, e questo ci dà fiducia per il futuro. Abbiamo giocatori di altissimo livello. Abbiamo copertura in alcune posizioni, un po' meno in altre, ma abbiamo tempo", ha detto.

#2184. Infortuni Serie A, solo la Juve di Spalletti peggio del Napoli di Allegri: il dato

La squadra con più partite saltate dai propri giocatori per infortunio in questo inizio di stagione di Serie A è la Juventus, sulla quale però pesano gli stop traumatici rispetto a quelli di entità muscolare: Locatelli è stato operato al menisco esterno, Yildiz al piede sinistro, Grabara al ginocchio destro, Khéphren Thuram anche. I numeri raccontano di 70 partite saltate, dieci in più del Napoli, la seconda squadra più colpita.

A raccontarlo è la Gazzetta dello Sport: “Qui la questione è ben diversa, perché salvo lo stop del lungodegente Buongiorno (anche lui operato al menisco), i problemi accusati dai vari Badiashile, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Spinazzola e compagnia sono tutti di natura muscolare e quindi più iscrivibili alle possibili cause che abbiamo elencato”.

Al terzo posto l’Atalanta, con 57 partite saltate, numeri alti anche per Sassuolo (55), le neopromosse Venezia (50) e Monza (47) e Genoa (46), mentre il Frosinone è la squadra meno colpita (13).

#2183. Nicky Hayen eyed by new club after Burnley exit

Burnley cut ties with the Belgian at the end of last month after a poor start to the Championship season. He was replaced by Fabio Celestini at Turf Moor.

Hayen, 46, was appointed by the Clarets in the summer after their relegation from the Premier League but he struggled to adapt to life in Lancashire. He won only one of his 14 matches at the helm before he was eventually given the chop following a 4-1 away defeat at Lincoln City.

In this latest update regarding his situation, the Press and Journal claim he has emerged on the radar of Aberdeen up in Scotland as they look to bring in a new head coach. They have recently parted ways with ex-Oldham Athletic and Morecambe man Stephen Robinson and they are in the hunt for someone new.

Burnley drew with both Portsmouth and QPR after Hayen’s departure before their frantic 5-4 loss against Cardiff City in South Wales last time out before the international break. They are back in action next Sunday with an away trip to Ewood Park to play rivals Blackburn Rovers.

Hayen was the wrong man for Burnley and wasn’t able to get a tune out of their squad. He arrived in England as a bit of an unknown quantity back in July.

The Clarets handed him a three-year deal running until June 2029. Celestini has now been left to pick up the pieces though and faces a tough job.

Burnley are in the drop zone along with Preston North End and Derby County. They are five points from safety behind both Lincoln City and Watford after their disappointing collapse at the Cardiff City Stadium.

Prior to his switch, Hayen spent seven months at Genk. He has also had spells in the past in his native Belgium at Sint-Truidense VV, SK Beveren and Club Brugge, as well as having a stint in Wales at Haverfordwest County.

A change of scene to Aberdeen would be good for Hayen. It can provide him with a fresh start and a new opportunity to prove himself.

The Dons are 11th in the league and risk slipping into the Scottish Championship if they aren’t careful. They have won three of their opening 12 matches and are two points above Kilmarnock at the bottom who they play up next.

#2181. Lotito e Fabiani vogliono blindare Gattuso, ma il tecnico pretende garanzie sul mercato

Lotito e Fabiani spingono per il 2029, ma Gattuso chiede prima un aumento per i collaboratori e garanzie sui big.

Approfittando della sosta, a Formello è tempo di programmare il futuro. La dirigenza laziale si muove per consolidare il progetto, convinta dal lavoro di Gattuso dopo un avvio di stagione straordinario che vede attualmente i biancocelesti al primo posto in classifica.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Stando a quanto rivelato oggi da Il Messaggero, Lotito e Fabiani si sono mossi per blindare Gennaro Gattuso prolungando l'accordo fino al 2029. L'attuale intesa estiva prevede 1,2 milioni di euro con opzione legata al piazzamento fino al 2028. Nonostante le sirene dei top club d'Europa, Gattuso non brama ritocchi personali, concentrandosi piuttosto sui suoi collaboratori: i circa 700 mila euro complessivi suddivisi tra i nove membri dello staff appaiono infatti insufficienti rispetto ai meriti e ai traguardi raggiunti finora.

Prima di firmare il rinnovo a gennaio, il tecnico vuole risposte chiare sul mercato e sulle reali possibilità d'azione della società, che deve prima sistemare i conti in bilancio entro il 30 novembre. Lotito e Fabiani hanno promesso che nessun big partirà a gennaio, neanche di fronte a offerte pazzesche, ma l'allenatore prima di crederci vuole vedere fatti concreti.

#2178. Lazio, Canigiani svela le novità: biglietti del derby e nuovo sponsor tecnico

Il direttore marketing della Lazio fa il punto su derby e Supercoppa e svela a che punto è la scelta dello sponsor tecnico.

Novità importanti sul fronte Lazio, sia per quanto riguarda i biglietti del derby sia per il futuro sponsor tecnico. Marco Canigiani, direttore marketing biancoceleste, ha fatto il punto sulla situazione, soffermandosi anche sulla vendita dei tagliandi per la Supercoppa.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Sul derby, il dato fornito da Canigiani parla di 16-17mila biglietti già venduti. Considerando anche gli abbonati, i posti occupati si stanno avvicinando a quota 25mila. Dalla prossima settimana, inoltre, la vendita verrà estesa ai possessori delle Fidelity Card.

Novità anche sullo sponsor tecnico. Con Mizuno attualmente in scadenza a fine anno, la Lazio è arrivata al rush finale: sono arrivate diverse offerte e il club ne ha già selezionate un paio. Il marchio giapponese mantiene però un diritto di prelazione.

Secondo quanto riportato da Radiosei, Marco Canigiani ha spiegato nel dettaglio le diverse fasi previste dal club.

Il direttore marketing ha spiegato come si sta sviluppando la prima fase della vendita:

“In questa momento è attiva una fase che abbiamo voluto dedicare agli abbonati della passata stagione, prelazione che non può essere sul posto in cui erano abbonati o nel settore perché magari è stato occupato, ma solo loro possono acquistare in questo momento. Un abbonato può acquistare fino a 4 biglietti, sempre per gli abbonati della scorsa stagione. Dalla prossima settimana la possibilità si amplierà ai possessori delle Fidelity Card, anche loro potranno acquistare fino a 4 biglietti sempre per chi possiede le varie card”.

L'intenzione della Lazio è favorire il più possibile la presenza dei propri sostenitori:

“L’obiettivo ovviamente è preferire la vendita ai nostri tifosi, soprattutto per la Monte Mario; per la Tevere, anche più avanti servirà, la Eagle Card, mentre in Monte Mario partirà la vendita libera, che quindi ci auguriamo sia limitata. La Roma avrà il settore Sud e una iniziale dotazione di Monte Mario sud, poi è chiaro che della vendita libera ne può usufruire chiunque. Le card devono essere retroattive, altrimenti quello che è l’obiettivo poteva essere facilmente aggirabile. Le card hanno un prezzo irrisorio, quindi non sarebbero una barriera. Può acquistare ora chi quindi aveva le card già prima dell’inizio della vendita. Noi al momento abbiamo oltre 16-17mila biglietti. Siamo intorno ai 20mila presenti più gli abbonati, quindi ci avviciniamo ai 25mila posti occupati. Nei Distinti c’è ancora qualche disponibilità”.

Canigiani ha poi sottolineato il potenziale della fase riservata ai possessori delle tessere:

“Potenzialmente i possessori di tessere potrebbero riempiro lo stadio, dipende dalla volontà di farlo; anzi potrebbero anche non bastare i posti. Il biglietto deve essere intestato al possessore delle card nella fase che scatterà lunedì. L’obiettivo è quello di arrivare alla vendita libera con meno posti a disposizione“.

Capitolo Supercoppa: bisognerà attendere le comunicazioni della Lega per conoscere ufficialmente date e modalità di vendita.

“Supercoppa? A breve la Lega comunicherà date e modalità di vendita, anche qui abbiamo previsto diverse fasi. Credo che già la prossima settimana potrà iniziare la vendita. Lo stadio, essendo una gara della Lega, è diviso a metà. Entrambe le card avranno una fase dedicata”.

#2177. Osmajic e Varela saranno i 9 più cercati della Serie A a gennaio

Milutin Osmajic del Genoa e Gustavo Varela sono i due uomini centrali nel calciomercato delle due squadre per il mercato di gennaio. Riusciranno i club a non scontentare Daniele De Rossi e Ivan Juric? Le parole degli ultimi giorni, dell'agente del giocatore e della dirigenza dei brianzoli, lasciano intendere due fattori: che le società faranno di tutto per tenerli ma che, altrettanto... Deciderà il mercato e le offerte che arriveranno.

Ne parliamo nel Podcast di oggi di Tuttomercatoweb.com in compagnia di Marco Conterio

Nel corso dell'intervista rilasciata a TuttoMercatoWeb.com l'agente di Milutin Osmajic, Igor Gluscevic, nel ribadire quanto il proprio assistito si stia trovando bene al Genoa ha risposto in merito all'ipotesi che qualche grande squadra possa interessarsi a lui già nel mercato di gennaio. Ecco le sue parole. "Non mi sorprende affatto. A dire il vero, me lo aspettavo. Era già prontissimo tre anni fa, prima ancora di trasferirsi in Inghilterra. Ai tempi del Vizela, le sue migliori prestazioni le ha offerte proprio contro Benfica, Sporting e Porto. Ha vissuto tre anni fantastici in Championship, segnando oltre 50 gol ufficiali, un bottino incredibile e impressionante in 100 presenze (nonostante ne abbia saltate 30 in tre stagioni per via di circostanze ben note). Se si osservano tutti i gol realizzati in Portogallo, in Inghilterra e con la nazionale, è chiaro che quanto sta accadendo non è affatto una sorpresa. Il suo valore era già noto in passato, ma per varie ragioni non si è concretizzato nulla; il Preston, forte di un contratto a lungo termine, chiedeva una cifra coerente con il suo valore, tra i 10 e i 15 milioni di euro. Andare altrove a gennaio? Il giocatore è pronto. La decisione spetta al Genoa. Un affare si considera tale quando tutte le parti coinvolte sono soddisfatte".

Il Corriere dello Sport fa il punto sul mercato di gennaio in attacco del Napoli e sulla volontà della società di rivedere il reparto offensivo, con più di un’uscita possibile già nella finestra invernale. Le partenze di Noa Lang, Lorenzo Lucca e David Neres libererebbero spazio e risorse per gli innesti per dare nuova linfa all’attacco di Max Allegri.

#2175. Sheffield United summer signing scores in 4-0 win on international captaincy debut

Bangladesh ran out as 4-0 winners over Sri Lanka to progress to the semi-finals of the SAFF Championship, where they will lock horns with Pakistan. After Shamit Shome broke the deadlock inside nine minutes, Sheffield United man Hamza Choudhury was on hand to double the lead.

The SUFC man ventured forward with a darting run in behind the defence before emphatically slotting home.

Further goals from Boreham Wood’s Farhaan Ali Wahid – currently on loan from Fulham – and Rakib Hossain put the finishing touches on a convincing victory in the second half. It made it back-to-back victories for Bangladesh for the first time since 2023.

A former England U21s international, Choudhury stepped in to lead the team for the first time in the absence of long-serving captain Jamal Bhuyan.

Ex-Leicester City and Watford man Choudhury changed allegiance from England to Bangladesh in December of 2024, a move which is beginning to pay dividends.

His debut came in March last year against India, before netting his first goal in a 2-0 win over Bhutan just over two months later. Choudhury now adds another feather to his international cap by captaining his country for the first time.

Switching allegiance to Bangladesh marked a significant turning point for the South Asian nation, with Choudhury becoming their first player to play in the Premier League. He has been hailed as the figurehead to drive forward a country not renowned for its football exploits.

After a damaging 9-2 defeat to Indonesia, which saw them crash out of the FIFA ASEAN Cup in the last international break, Choudhury’s side have bounced back in perfect fashion and he has been at the heart of that.

Deployed in both his conventional midfield role as well as at right-back, the former Burton Albion loanee will be pivotal if they are to end their 23-year wait for an international title in the SAFF Championship.

While his form on the international stage has gone to another level, Choudhury has lacked consistency at Sheffield United this term.

The 29-year-old put pen to paper on a permanent deal at Bramall Lane following a successful loan stint and has been a mainstay at right-back after Femi Seriki was ruled out for the season with a patellar tendon rupture.

He produced impressive displays in their three-game unbeaten run, victories over Preston North End and Wrexham and a draw with Derby County, but he was taken off at half-time in their latest defeat to Charlton Athletic.

Given Seriki’s absence, Choudhury will be keen to regain his best form and will need to do so if SUFC are to enter the Championship play-off conversation, with his recent exploits for Bangladesh potentially providing the confidence to reignite his season.

#2174. Elezioni FIGC, Galliani vince: la verifica delle candidature spetta al segretario generale

la competenza sulla verifica dell’ammissibilità delle candidature alla presidenza federale spetta esclusivamente al segretario generale della FIGC

Vittoria per Adriano Galliani nella controversia sulla commissione elettorale della FIGC. Secondo quanto riportato da Calcio e Finanza, l’iniziativa promossa da Galliani davanti al Tribunale federale nazionale ha raggiunto il suo obiettivo: chiarire che la competenza sulla verifica dell’ammissibilità delle candidature alla presidenza federale spetta esclusivamente al segretario generale della FIGC, Marco Brunelli, e non alla commissione istituita dal commissario straordinario Giovanni Malagò.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il risultato è emerso in occasione dell’udienza tenutasi nella mattinata di venerdì 13 novembre. La commissione ha chiarito di avere esclusivamente un ruolo consultivo, senza alcun potere autonomo di verifica e decisione sull’ammissibilità delle candidature. Una precisazione che ha permesso a Galliani di raggiungere il risultato perseguito con la propria iniziativa, riportando al centro della procedura elettorale le competenze attribuite dalle norme federali al segretario generale.

#2173. Lazio, per Sutalo il derby è andato. Lesione di secondo grado, il 2026 potrebbe essere finito

L’infortunio di Josip Sutalo, rimediato a Napoli, si sta rivelando più serio del previsto: la lesione al flessore appare molto più vicina al secondo grado che al primo (circa 45 giorni di stop), e la sua presenza al derby del 13 dicembre è ormai da considerarsi quasi impossibile. La vera corsa contro il tempo riguarda semmai un altro appuntamento, la finale di Supercoppa Italiana contro l’Inter, in programma il 22 dicembre a San Siro, fa sapere oggi Il Tempo.

Inoltre si è fermato di nuovo Marusic: è allarme in difesa. Gattuso sicuramente dovrà sciogliere un dubbio non banale per completare la coppia centrale al fianco di Provstgaard. Le opzioni portano entrambe ai due ex Union Berlino: con Doekhi si tornerebbe alla coppia titolare dell’avvio di stagione, quella che aveva convinto nelle prime giornate; con Diogo Leite si formerebbe invece una coppia anomala, composta da due mancini, anche se il portoghese, ogni volta che è stato chiamato in causa, ha sempre garantito prestazioni di qualità. Resta infine una terza suggestione, utile solo nel caso in cui sia Provstgaard a dover rifiatare: il ritorno del duo Doekhi-Diogo Leite, coppia che aveva già funzionato ai tempi dell’Union Berlino. Entrambi, va ricordato, sono arrivati alla Lazio da svincolati la scorsa estate, Doekhi a fine luglio e Diogo Leite nei primi giorni di settembre.

#2172. ‘Definitely’: Birmingham City reporter delivers Chris Davies contract verdict amid impressive turnaround

Birmingham City have won six of their last seven Championship games to surge to the top of the table after 15 matches. BCFC are in a fine position as the November international break continues, and the work of Chris Davies has drawn significant praise.

There have been doubts over his Blues future at times, especially during a disappointing 2025/26 season, but Davies has completed an impressive turnaround to secure his position. And, one man who believes the Welshman’s work should be rewarded with a new deal is Birmingham Live’s Alex Dicken.

When quizzed on Davies’ contract situation in a fan Q&A, Blues reporter Dicken wrote: “I think they should give it a few months to allow the relationship between John Murtough (Birmingham City’s new director of football) and Davies to develop – and get the transfer window done and dusted – but it’s definitely something that should be looked at before the end of the season.

“I think Chris Davies is the sort of manager who will want security and to know where he stands. It is remarkable what he’s done in the last six months when you consider he faced questions over his future at the club in March/April last year. He has shown huge development as a young manager.”

Davies started strongly as he led a strong Birmingham City side to a rampant League One title win. That was expected though, so the boss and his side rose to the Championship with a point to prove.

And, they failed to prove it. Last season, BCFC struggled for consistency and frustrated their supporters with football that was often drab and unimaginative. It led to calls for Davies to be replaced by a bigger name, but the hierarchy stuck by their boss.

There were some lingering doubts early this season, but the doubters have been silenced with a stunning surge to the summit of the Championship. Birmingham City play with much more speed and impetus in possession, as shown by the fact that they have scored 21 goals in the last 10 games. They’ve maintained defensive solidity too though, with Christoph Klarer and Phil Neumann starring.

Davies was criticised for not adapting or getting the best out of City’s attacking talents last season. He has done both of those things this term though, highlighting his own development and growth as a boss.

Davies dealt with the pressure of turning around Birmingham City’s fortunes. But, such is the ambition of the club that he must now take on the task of maintaining their impressive form.

BCFC have eyes on a rise to the Premier League with a new stadium on the horizon and dreams of a Jude Bellingham return remaining for Tom Wagner.

Davies’ importance in this cannot be overstated, and further security over his future would be richly deserved. His current contract runs until 2028, so entrusting him with the next stage of their project means a new contract will be required.

As Dicken argues though, perhaps it is best to wait until new director of football Murtough is settled. If a relationship can be built between the two, an agreement becomes even more logical.

#2170. Man City star signs - What Charlton Athletic’s perfect January transfer window looks like

Charlton Athletic find themselves set for a hard-fought relegation battle down in the Championship and it could well be that good business done in the January transfer window is what saves them.

Having started the season with three successive victories and then a draw away at promotion challenging West Bromwich Albion at The Hawthorns, things looked as though they were on the up for Charlton.

Having survived the drop in their first season back in the second-tier last season, the expectation within the fanbase would have been to kick on this year and the start suggested that they will.

However, The Addicks then endured a ten-match winless run of form which only ended just before the international break with a 2-1 defeat of Sheffield United at The Valley.

Joint lowest scorers in the division, it is clear that Charlton need a spark in the final third and a general shift around in their squad and so we have taken a look at what would be an ideal winter window for the South Londoners.

A bit of a gamble but someone who could be a major surprise point of difference for Charlton in the second half of the season would be Younes Ibrahim, if they can get Brighton and Hove Albion to agree to loan out their starlet in the winter.

A mobile attacking midfielder will be a key addition for Charlton this winter with plenty of players having been tried but underwhelmed in that position – and Ibrahim, while very inexperienced, could be someone to provide a much-needed spark.

Bolton Wanderers and Derby County should prepare bids for former Charlton Athletic target Jesurun Rak-Sakyi this January

Brighton youngsters thriving in the EFL would not be a new thing and is perhaps a model for many to follow, with Amario Cozier-Duberry the best example on loan at Middlesbrough after his impressive stint with Bolton Wanderers last season.

The 18-year-old Egyptian is the latest prodigy coming through at the AMEX Stadium and an exciting first-team debut against Kauno Zalgiris in their UEFA Europa Conference League league phase opener, in which he earned an assist in a 4-0 victory over the Lithuanian champions, may well be a prompt for some EFL interest this winter.

A bit more known and recognisable to EFL followers and Charlton supporters but someone who is only who is even younger than Ibrahim at 17 would be winger Jeremy Monga.

Monga came through at Coventry City and then Leicester City before making his Premier League debut at the age of just 15 for The Foxes in the 2024-25 campaign before featuring on 27 occasions in the Championship last season.

He joined Manchester City over the summer before being loaned out to Swansea City but the sheer quality and depth of attacking talent that the promotion challenging Jacks have has limited Monga to being on the bench, and remaining an unused substitute, on just three occasions this season.

Monga is surely destined to have that loan stint cut-short but a Championship move still remains the likelier option for him and Charlton are crying out for some exciting wide talent and pace.

Moving away from the recruitment of young starlets to provide a spark in the final third, Charlton may well require a poacher in order to finish off whatever creativity is sought and produced.

As a result, they could do a lot worse than moving for Reading’s 32-year-old striker Jack Marriott, who hasn’t played Championship football since the 2021-22 campaign when he scored nine goals in 28 appearances for Peterborough United.

He has remained a consistent threat in the EFL, notching 16 in 24 League One games for The Royals last season before racing to nine across all competitions this season, albeit with injuries often disrupting him. With Jacob Brown and Jamie Reid now in Berkshire, though, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Reading deem a sale, for any fee but surely a relatively low one given his age, acceptable.

Matty Godden has had critics this season, albeit he did score their winner against The Blades at the weekend, and finding an upgrade on his profile; an experienced finisher for the level could well be a priority for Charlton.

Zach Mitchell came through the Charlton academy setup in 2022 but the 21-year-old defender has only gone on to make 20 appearances across all competitions for the club with loan spells at Colchester United, Saint Johnstone twice and Hibernian in recent seasons.

Still young, it could well be that Mitchell moves away from The Valley on a temporary basis initially but out of contract next summer and without a squad number this season, his departure feels fairly inevitable at this stage.

Another defender who could well depart this winter would be Kenya international Collins Sichenje, who signed for Charlton from Serbian outfit Vojvodina in February.

The 23-year-old managed just six appearances in the second half of last season with just three starts. This time around, he came off the bench to defend 2-1 victories against Derby County and West Ham United in August but hasn’t been seen since in the league, with a couple of other substitute appearances in the EFL Cup and his departure would also feel quite likely.

Following their promotion in 2025, Charlton brought in a fair few attackers that had previously thrived at a lower level and many have failed to make too much of an impact and one of them is Harvey Knibbs.

The former Cambridge United and Reading man struggled to find form and consistency in the conservative approach and setup of Jones last season and he managed just two starts thus far this season in defeats against Middlesbrough and Bolton Wanderers. To free up space in attack and also for himself to get game-time, a move this winter would surely suit all parties.

#2169. Romano: “Rafa Marin? Il Napoli è soddisfatto, ma il rinnovo non è una priorità”

Il rinnovo di Rafa Marin non è urgente. Il Napoli ha fatto il punto sul futuro del difensore, ma al momento non c’è alcuna fretta di intervenire sul contratto. La società è soddisfatta del suo rendimento e preferisce non forzare i tempi, lasciando che il discorso maturi con calma. Lo fa sapere Fabrizio Romano.

Nei giorni scorsi il direttore sportivo Giovanni Manna ha incontrato l’entourage del giocatore, in un confronto che ha toccato anche il tema del rinnovo. Da quell’incontro non è emersa però alcuna accelerazione. Il Napoli ha scelto di rinviare ogni valutazione, senza fissare scadenze e senza aprire una vera trattativa. Un segnale di serenità, che racconta il rapporto positivo tra le parti e l’assenza di tensione sul futuro del calciatore.

La linea del club è dunque chiara: il rinnovo di Rafa Marin è un discorso da rinviare a dati da destinarsi. Per ora conta ciò che il difensore sta facendo in campo, e il Napoli è contento del suo contributo alla squadra. In un momento complicato per l’ambiente azzurro, con tanti temi di mercato aperti e diversi contratti in bilico, quello di Marin non rientra tra i dossier più caldi. La società preferisce dedicare energie alle priorità immediate, tenendo il difensore tra i punti fermi su cui costruire anche nei prossimi mesi, senza bisogno di decisioni affrettate.

#2168. Torna in campo Ronaldinho. Il giorno del suo arrivo in Italia in diretta

È ormai partito il conto alla rovescia per il ritorno in campo di Ronaldinho. Il fuoriclasse brasiliano è atteso oggi in Italia per unirsi al Ravenna in vista del derby di domenica contro il Forlì. Dopo undici anni lontano dalle partite ufficiali, il Pallone d'Oro si prepara a una nuova avventura in Serie C, con l'obiettivo di lasciare il segno anche in giallorosso. Segui su TMW tutti gli aggiornamenti in tempo reale sull'arrivo di Ronaldinho e sul suo ritorno in campo.

14.45 - Ronaldinho è atterrato in Italia Ronaldinho è arrivato in Italia! L'aereo che ha portato il fuoriclasse in Romagna è da poco atterrato all'aeroporto di Forlì. L'ex Pallone d'Oro, accolto da Ignazio Cipriani, ora si trasferirà a Milano Marittima dove resterà fino a lunedì, giorno della sua partenza. Oggi allenamento personalizzato, domani la rifinitura con il gruppo e domenica scenderà in campo nel derby Ravenna-Forlì.

12:35 - Quanto giocherà Ronaldinho? C'è grande curiosità intorno a Ronaldinho, soprattutto per la tenuta fisica. Quanto e come giocherà ce lo spiega direttamente il tecnico del Ravenna, Andrea Mandorlini, intervistato da Sky: "Entrerà nel secondo tempo e si metterà lì davanti. In che posizione? I campioni devono scegliere…”

12:05 - Ronaldinho atterra alle 15 Ronaldinho arriverà a Forlì intorno alle 15, con circa quattro ore di ritardo rispetto all'orario inizialmente previsto delle 11. Il fuoriclasse brasiliano atterrerà all'aeroporto Luigi Ridolfi e si trasferirà direttamente a Milano Marittima, dove soggiornerà nella suite di un hotel all'ottavo piano. Nel pomeriggio è in programma una seduta di allenamento personalizzata, mentre domani, alla vigilia del derby di Serie C, svolgerà il primo allenamento insieme ai compagni del Ravenna.

11:21 - Ronaldinho al Ravenna arriva anche a Times Square Il ritorno in campo di Ronaldinho ha già conquistato Times Square. L'evento che domenica vedrà protagonista il fuoriclasse brasiliano con la maglia del Ravenna ha trovato spazio anche a New York, dove, come mostrato dallo stesso club, le immagini del suo ritorno sono state trasmesse sui maxischermi della Nasdaq Tower. Un'eco internazionale che conferma l'attenzione attorno a una partita destinata probabilmente a diventare una delle più seguite nella storia della Serie C.

Visualizza questo post su Instagram Un post condiviso da Ravenna Football Club (@ravennafootballclub)

Un post condiviso da Ravenna Football Club (@ravennafootballclub)

10:26 - Un solo precedente per Ronaldinho in Romagna ai tempi del Milan, con il Cesena che fu in grado di imporsi 2-0 con reti di Bogdani e Giaccherini. Luca Ceccarelli, ex difensore del Cesena, racconta come ha fermato Dinho nell'unico precedente in Romagna del fuoriclasse brasiliano: "Non si doveva girare e io non mi dovevo far puntare. Per questo ho adottato un atteggiamento molto aggressivo. Tutta la squadra ha aggredito forte, in avanti, costantemente, senza paura. Sapevamo che Ronaldinho non curava la fase difensiva e io mi inserivo molto da dietro, quindi volevo essere il più preciso possibile nei cross per non farli ripartire".

09:47 - Cresce l'attesa anche fra i compagni di squadra, Duca: "È una leggenda" In casa Ravenna cresce l'attesa per il ritorno in campo di Ronaldinho, atteso domenica nel derby contro il Forlì. Tra i giocatori che avranno l'occasione di condividere il campo con il campione brasiliano c'è anche Edoardo Duca, centrocampista giallorosso, che ha raccontato al Corriere di Romagna le sensazioni dello spogliatoio in vista di un appuntamento speciale. "Il clima è sempre positivo, Ronaldinho è una leggenda e un plus per tutti noi, sarà una bella domenica per tutti gli appassionati di calcio del mondo, secondo me noi non realizzeremo il tutto fino al momento in cui lo avremo di fianco in campo. Allo stesso tempo sappiamo cosa ci aspetta domenica e per cosa andremo a giocare".

09:00 - Ronaldinho è atteso in Italia nella tarda mattinata di oggi e alloggerà per quattro giorni all'hotel Bolina di Milano Marittima. Nel pomeriggio svolgerà un allenamento personalizzato a porte chiuse, mentre domani alle 11 sarà al Benelli per la rifinitura insieme ai compagni del Ravenna. La seduta sarà blindata, ma i media accreditati potranno assistere ai primi 15 minuti. Domenica il debutto nel derby contro il Forlì.

#2167. The 16 players set to miss Sheffield Wednesday v Plymouth Argyle

The November international break means a reduced slate of League One action this weekend, but one of the key games still going ahead takes place at Hillsborough, as Sheffield Wednesday face Plymouth Argyle.

New Owls manager Dave Challinor takes charge of his first league game in South Yorkshire, looking to bounce back from defeats against League Two opposition in the FA Cup and the EFL Trophy in his first two games in charge, although the latter, against Accrington Stanley on Wednesday, featured many debutants and an inexperienced side.

Ultimately, the former Stockport County boss has been brought in to oversee a surge back up the League One table towards the automatic promotion places, but a match against Argyle presents somewhat of a baptism of fire.

Tom Cleverley's side head to Hillsborough with the second-best away record in the division and with the opportunity to open a six-point gap over their opponents, further cementing their own promotion credentials a third of the way through the campaign.

Both sides have been plagued by injury so far this season, though, and this Saturday will be no different. These 14 players won't be available for the battle at Hillsborough.

Despite having four players on international duty this weekend, Sheffield Wednesday don't have enough players who fall under the required quota to postpone a game. The biggest absence will be Kieran Morrison, who was called up by Northern Ireland.

The Liverpool loanee has started only one of Wednesday's last five league games, but won't be available on Saturday, with his focus instead on a Nations League outing with Ukraine later that evening.

Jordi Liongola made his return to action after missing a couple of months with a hamstring injury, just last weekend against Oldham in the FA Cup.

FLW gets ChatGPT to take a look at the roughest, most intimidating sets of fans in the third tier

However, his return to full fitness will now be managed by Burundi, who called him up for their meetings with Zambia in this month's AFCON qualifiers.

It was a proud moment for Sean Fusire on Wednesday night, as he captained the young Owls side in their EFL Trophy defeat against Accrington.

He'll now jet off to represent Zimbabwe in their AFCON qualifier double-header against Equatorial Guinea.

And the final international call-up sees Will Grainger represent the Wales Under-19 squad in their Euro qualifiers over the coming weeks.

The 17-year-old came off the bench to help Wales to a 2-2 draw against Finland on Wednesday night, and will face both Spain and Iceland in the coming week.

Onto the injury list, and Dave Challinor will have a big decision to make at left-back this weekend, with both of his recognised senior names currently sidelined, the first of which is Max Lowe.

The 29-year-old is one of the more experienced high-level names in the Wednesday squad this season, but has struggled to remain fit for lengthy periods in recent years. He'll be out for four to six weeks after re-aggravating an earlier injury against Oldham last weekend.

Backup left-back Reece James also continues to miss action after being left out of the last two games in all competitions.

The groin issue he picked up shouldn't see him back in action until mid-December.

There was some good news on the injury front on Wednesday, with Dave Challinor revealing that four key players could return, one of whom is the Owls' number one, Joe Lumley.

That's helpful, as the Owls were forced to play third-choice shot-stopper Connal Trueman for the majority of their FA Cup exit at Oldham and the entirety of Wednesday's Trophy defeat, as Ashley Maynard-Brewer was forced off with a bang to the head at Boundary Park.

Mason Burstow was starting to get a head of steam in the Wednesday fold under caretaker boss Matt Hamshaw, starting both games under him, scoring against Cambridge United and looking lively throughout.

Therefore, it was quite typical that the Hull City loanee would be sidelined afterwards, with Dave Challinor suggesting that the groin injury he picked up against Blackpool was due to him shooting from the halfway line. He'll miss four to six weeks.

Ali Al-Hamadi would usually be away on international duty with Iraq, but was forced to miss the squad this time around after picking up a foot injury towards the back end of October.

His return date is unknown, but the Sheffield Star indicates that next Friday's meeting with Barnsley is the target.

Tyler Onyango's crushing history of knee injuries during the infancy of his career reared its ugly head just 14 minutes into his Wednesday debut on the opening day at Leyton Orient.

The 23-year-old is set to miss the remainder of the campaign.

#2166. Bolton & Cardiff should pounce on Sunderland striker Timur Tutierov

The January transfer window is looming into view and clubs across the EFL will be seeking to strengthen their squads in order to secure their goals in the second half of the season.

Two teams that are expected to be active are Bolton Wanderers and Cardiff City, who should both be aiming to bring in Sunderland striker Timur Tutierov this winter.

Both Bolton and Cardiff gained promotion back to the second-tier last season and they have both been competitive in the Championship, heading into the November international break sitting 14th and 18th respectively.

Bolton missed the chance to close in on the top half as they succumbed to a 3-1 defeat away at Derby County last week, having been ahead at half-time, but they remain a respectable seven points clear of the bottom three and the relegation places after winning the League One play-offs in May.

As for Cardiff, The Bluebirds’ performances may well have supporters believing they could have a tilt at the top eight and the expanded play-off spots. Goal scoring issues may not be forefront of their mind right now after coming from 4-1 down to beat Burnley at the weekend, a few days after giving up a three-goal lead to draw with West Ham United.

Both have laid a foundation for themselves and adding some extra depth and quality this winter could be key to their end of season aspirations – and Tutierov may well be a promising market opportunity for either.

Ukraine U21 international Timur Tutierov joined Sunderland from Ukrainian Premier League outfit Kolos Kovalivka in the summer of 2023 and it is only now that the 21-year-old forward is beginning to get first-team football at the Stadium of Light.

Capable of playing out-wide, Tutierov, who spent the second half of last season on loan at Exeter City in League One, has been linked with a move to Blackburn Rovers, too, recently.

Tutierov has benefitted from Sunderland having a small squad and injuries to strikers Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor, as well as Regis Le Bris not yet trusting summer signing Juan Riquelme Angulo, has prompted a rapid promotion to the first-team picture for the Ukrainian on Wearside.

Tutierov has continued to feature for Sunderland’s U21 side, and he even got a goal and an assist against Accrington Stanley in the EFL Trophy earlier this season, while filling in for the likes of Isidor and Brobbey.

Tutierov made his first Sunderland start in the UEFA Europa League last month as The Black Cats defeated Portuguese second-tier outfit Torreense away from home before he scored his first European goal for the club in their next game, a 1-1 draw with Lech Poznan in Poland.

Domestically, Tutierov has made two Premier League appearances, including a start against AFC Bournemouth a few weeks ago, as well as having played in both of their EFL Cup games thus far; again scoring in a 3-2 victory over Brentford in the fourth round.

Sunderland supporters have questioned Le Bris’ decision-making at times this season and there are question marks over the viability of Tutierov’s long-term future in the first-team picture but the Ukrainian has certainly shown some signs of promise in terms of his finishing and his ability to be a nuisance for a struggling side.

However, as Brobbey returns to full fitness and Haiti international striker Isidor also makes his comeback, there is an expectation that Tutierov is pushed out on loan again this winter, especially if Sunderland again reinforce their squad up-front, and Championship clubs should be ready to take a punt.

For much of the summer, Bolton pursued former Milton Keynes Dons striker Max Dean and it looked as though The Trotters were about to get a deal over the line before the close of the summer transfer window.

However, Dean’s move eventually collapsed and Wanderers instead only brought in Ryan Hardie on loan from Wrexham and Theo Bair on loan from Auxerre as an out and out striker to support Sam Dalby up-front.

A look at the 25 biggest clubs in England according to AI chatbot ChatGPT.

Hardie has badly struggled in his brief cameos for The Whites, while Bair has shown flashes of quality but a general inconsistency as well as being almost too similar a profile to main man Dalby in attack.

Another striker is a must for Steven Schumacher this winter and a striker of a different profile, one in which they can be a threat with runs in behind and off the ball, would be key.

Given his ability to play out-wide and with a bit of speed, Tutierov would surely fit that bill and, as he continued to gain some much-needed high-level experience, Bolton may well be the beneficiaries of a breakthrough season for the former Kolos man.

Cardiff have a well set and impressive style of football implemented by coach Brian Barry-Murphy and their style of football has not been short of goals with nine scored in their last two games against teams playing in the Premier League last season.

A theme of Barry-Murphy’s reign has been a trust in the youth setup and few signings have been made in his three transfer windows in charge, albeit the sheer volume of academy graduates has meant they have not remained short up-front.

Versatility is another key with plenty of players having played in a variety of positions for the Northern Irishman and that extends to up-front with the versatile Callum Robinson adept at filling in for first-choice striker Yousef Salech - though he's been banished in recent weeks.

Salech hasn’t been at his most efficient best this season but he has remained a threat and goals have started to come for the Dane, who like Dalby, would remain the main man if Tutierov was to sign.

What is required, though, is that depth up-front with only three players scoring more than twice in the Championship so far this season for Cardiff – one being Salech, another being winger Ollie Tanner and the other the all-action attacker that is Jack Moylan.

In terms of another out and out striker, Cardiff don’t really possess one and, while Tutierov can play wide which would be another virtue in a Barry-Murphy side, adding extra depth to sustain themselves in the second-tier feels like a necessity.

#2165. QPR must take January action over 24-year-old who has not made a league appearance since August: Opinion

QPR refined their squad with a handful of incomings and outgoings in the summer transfer window. It has yielded good results at Loftus Road, but some of those who headed out the exit door have not found the fortunes they would have hoped for.

Among those in that category is goalkeeper Joe Walsh. The 24-year-old saw a loan move away from West London sanctioned, with Pierce Charles becoming the new No. 1 while on loan from Manchester City and new signing Calum Ward locking down the spot as his backup.

Walsh was sent to League One with Wigan Athletic, but things have unravelled fairly quickly for him in the North West. And, having lost his starting berth, QPR should be recalling him when the winter transfer window comes around.

Walsh took the No. 1 shirt upon arrival at Wigan Athletic and looked poised to be their starting ‘keeper. However, a tough start to the season saw the Latics lose their first three League One games while conceding six goals in the process, and they were knocked out of the Carabao Cup too.

Then, just before the end of the transfer window, Joe Whitworth was signed from Crystal Palace. The 22-year-old has since locked down the place as Gary Caldwell‘s starting shot-stopper, leaving Walsh to watch on from the bench in every league match since.

The difference in their stats is rather glaring. It must be noted that Walsh’s numbers are from a smaller sample size, but he recorded a save rate of just 40% compared to Whitworth’s 69.8%, and the QPR loanee’s xG prevented sits at -2.03 compared to Whitworth’s impressive +4.45 (all stats via FotMob).

In truth, Whitworth’s importance in goal means it feels unlikely that Walsh will reclaim his place. He has started in the EFL Trophy games – all of which have ended in victory – but the Hoops man was on the bench for the FA Cup clash at Boreham Wood.

The purpose of Walsh’s loan move away from QPR was to find game time. However, evidence shows he is not finding the opportunities needed.

He did not play for the Hoops before joining the Latics, so would not be restricted by the two-club rule. As such, the Championship side should look to send the goalkeeper out again.

A drop to League Two could offer Walsh the starting berth he desires. Opportunities in Scotland could also prove fruitful as he bids to find the game time he needs to develop.

#2164. Tom Wagner must plot Birmingham City transfer for Brentford’s ‘top talent’ who Jurgen Klopp loved

Birmingham City's ambitions of reaching the Premier League could very much come true in this Championship season, with Chris Davies' side making an extremely impressive start to the campaign.

For the first time in 18 years, Blues currently top the Championship on goal difference after taking 29 points from their first 15 games whilst also boasting the division's meanest defensive record.

Such exploits should also take nothing away from the fact Davies' men have looked streets ahead this season compared to last in terms of their attacking efficiency, which, in large parts, is down to a tactical rethink which was brought about during a five-game unbeaten streak which closed out 2025/26.

Davies revealed in pre-season that his side needed to score at least 70 times in 46 games to stand a chance of being deemed promotion contenders, and they have already found target 28 times, an average of 1.9 per game.

With the January transfer window looming, it has already been debated what activity will be conducted at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park, but one particular deal could unlock the keys to promotion.

It was recently explained by newly-appointed director of football, John Murtough, that should an opportunity to add quality to the current Blues squad arise, those in B9 would be "ready to react."

Although the aforementioned figures showcase that goals have been flying in from all angles for Davies' side this season, more firepower could be needed to ensure they keep up their momentum, as well as the added bonus of depth.

Birmingham are in the mix to win promotion this season and they should target an ambitious deal for Blackburn's Andri Gudjohnsen in January.

Ambition is also a buzzword often associated with the Midlands side right now, and whilst not every high-profile transfer made under Knighthead's ownership has paid dividends, a swoop for Brentford playmaker, Fabio Carvalho, could benefit all parties in January.

The Portuguese was signed from Liverpool two summers ago in a deal worth £27.5m on a five-year contract, but due to fitness issues, the 24-year-old is yet to fully make his mark at the Gtech Community Stadium despite a tally of eight goals in 35 appearances.

Carvalho's career still has many years to go, and few have lost sight of the technical qualities the former England and Portuguese youth international could bring to any side, particularly at Championship level or even beyond.

In 2021/22, the attacker enjoyed a stellar breakthrough season with Fulham, with his 10 goals and eight assists in just 36 second tier outings enough to earn a nomination for the division's Young Player of the Season award, which was eventually won by Brennan Johnson.

Such form alerted the attention of Liverpool, who acquired his services for a bargain £7.5m, with Jürgen Klopp quick to offer rave reviews.

Blues fans, would Fabio Carvalho be an ideal January signing? Comment below!

"What a talent he is, hey? A player who can bring a stadium to its feet," said the current German national team boss.

"He puts his personality into his performances, he is confident and adventurous with the ball, and he wants to make things happen. He is a versatile player for sure and is very much an attacking threat with his creativity and dynamism.

Carvalho later reminded everyone about his qualities at Championship level, scoring nine goals in just 20 appearances for Hull City in 2023/24 before signing for the Bees.

Having been held back in his progress through a serious ACL injury and further issues, regular minutes are a must for the playmaker, and Birmingham's current style would certainly get the best out of the playmaker.

When at his very best, Carvalho has struck fear into opposition defenders with his unpredictability and direct nature - a theme which currently runs through Birmingham's attack, showcased by the recent form of Liam Millar and Patrick Roberts on the flanks, as well as a vast improvement to Jay Stansfield's all-round game.

Whilst adjusting well to the 'number 10' role, Stansfield has since netted three times in his past two games when returning to the focal attacking role due to an injury sustained by August Priske, which will give Davies plenty to think about.

Carvalho is still under contract with Brentford until 2029, but as recently as January, it was claimed that a potential permanent exit was being discussed.

Whether such feelings are being debated by Keith Andrews at present remains to be seen, but his addition to Birmingham's frontline, if he avoids further issues, would be a significant statement of intent, although an alternative option could be a second swoop for Anis Mehmeti of Ipswich Town, who snubbed a Championship return in the summer window.

#2161. Steven Schumacher confirms Bolton Wanderers boost

Bolton Wanderers boss Steven Schumacher has no long-term concerns about club captain Eoin Toal and expects to see him back from his current setback around Christmas.

The 27-year-old Northern Ireland international is currently recovering from an ankle injury he picked up in a training session he picked up ahead of their 3-2 defeat against Bristol City in late October. He's missed the last three games.

Toal has had a history of ankle problems dating back to the 2023 EFL Trophy final. This is said to be an issue with the opposite ankle, but it adds to the narrative amongst some Bolton supporters that the centre-back can't stay fit for lengthy spells.

Since arriving at the Toughsheet Stadium in the summer of 2022, Toal has played 155 times for the Trotters, but only managed 22 league games in his first season and 19 in 2024/25. Despite a decent injury record in the past couple of years, though, this setback has raised some alarm bells, which Schumacher was quick to quieten.

Toal missed the majority of Steven Schumacher's first half-season at the club, after he arrived in late January 2025. In his first full campaign in charge, though, the 27-year-old was nearly ever-present.

The Northern Irishman missed the play-off final win over Stockport County with a hamstring injury, but before then, he made 39 league and play-off appearances, while also being left on the bench four times. Indeed, he missed only six games, including that Wembley final.

Then this season, when Toal wasn't playing, he was unused from the bench. This setback is his first this year, and his first lengthy one in terms of missing consecutive games since the 2024/25 campaign. Therefore, Schumacher isn't concerned about his long-term fitness.

"I think he will be fine – I mean, last year he played virtually every game up until the play-off semi-final,” Schumacher said, per the Bolton News. "He was available for pretty much every week and had overcome the injuries he had the previous season when we first came in.

"He had been really stop-start that first season, but I think he did enough to show that his body is durable, and I think he has been excellent for us. Injuries can happen; that’s football, but no, I don’t have any long-term concerns with Toally."

The Bolton boss was quick to outline that his recent injuries haven't been a recurrence of one issue, and his current ankle problem is "innocuous."

Ultimately, it's a perception that will follow Toal throughout the rest of his time at Bolton, even if this proves to be his only slightly major setback in the last two seasons.

#2160. Bristol City & West Ham ticketing twist has caused a huge backlash

West Ham have enforced a major ticketing decision involving away supporters ahead of next month's home clash against Bristol City - and it's causing quite the reaction online.

Following West Ham's unprecedented relegation from the Premier League back in May, the London Stadium represents the away day for away fans throughout the Championship.

Indeed, the second-tier has never seen a larger ground than the London Stadium's 60,000-capacity, and for virtually every fanbase, an away trip to this corner of East London is one of the most notable fixtures on the calendar all season.

Fans of Bristol City, however, have just received a fresh twist that will impact their fixture away to West Ham next month, with the decision stirring up mixed reaction among supporters online.

Bristol City fans will be ticking off a major Championship away day when they travel to West Ham on December 12, though trips to Middlesbrough, West Bromwich Albion and Derby County are all on the agenda before their journey down the M4 and into East London.

But it has come with a twist that will now see a reduced number of supporters in attendance within the London Stadium away end, with West Ham having reciprocated the Robins' travelling allocation.

A ticketing announcement from the West Country outfit has confirmed this, disclosing that tickets will be on sale to supporters from next Wednesday before revealing the allocation.

Now, the Robins have informed fans that they have received an allocation of just 2,110 tickets including rail seats and general seating. This, of course, is a fairly sizeable reduction on the Hammers' typical away allocation to travelling supporters of around 3,000, yet they've simply reciprocated what City have already done.

Football League World assesses and ranks the FIFTEEN best away fanbases in the EFL right now

The development comes following an announcement in September which revealed that Bristol City have opened the Atyeo Stand to home fans for high-profile fixtures against West Ham, Stoke and Severnside rivals Cardiff, thus reducing the number of tickes available to away supporters.

Therefore, West Ham have reacted by reducing their own allocation for the Robins faithful, and unsurprisingly, it's sparked something of a stir.

With every other Championship club to have travelled to West Ham so far this season having received a larger allocation, fans were quick to react following the Robins' announcement.

A lot of the reaction actually came from Hammers supporters, who wasted no time in lauding their club's reciprocal efforts.

This one fan, for example, applauded his side and urged them to do the same for every game against an opposing club that doesn't provide the same allocation.

Another, meanwhile, kept it direct and straight-to-the-point in response to a Bristol City punter who had questioned the allocation.

Indeed, this West Ham supporter believes the decision is evidence of the East Londoners actually getting something right, with many simply all-too-happy to see that their club has refused to simply roll over and give out the largest possible allocations while being restricted in some of their own travels on the road.

By contrast, Bristol City fans have naturally failed to share the same sentiment and believe that the Robins have been hard done by with this particular decision.

A Robins supporter here pulled no punches by describing it as an "absolute joke" - to which the Hammers' lot were, of course, swift in reminding of why the allocation has been shaved.

Emojis can sometimes tell the story, too, and in this case, they summed up exactly how another supporter of the Ashton Gate side is feeling right now.

However, another punter saw sense behind West Ham's decision and has backed the reciprocation.

There has been a split of opinion over West Ham's allocation for the travelling Bristol City contingent next month, even if many do believe that the Hammers are perfectly within their right to match the reduction.

However, there's absolutely no division when it comes to the prices that West Ham are charging for Robins fans who intend on making the trip to the London Stadium, which may just work out among their cheapest away days all season.

Adult tickets come cheaper than virtually anywhere else in the Championship at just £25, whereas 66+ and under-21 ones are even more affordable at a price of £12.

Under-18 tickets, meanwhile, will cost no more than £10, with these prices across the board paling in comparison to some other second-tier clubs.

It's also no shock that one West Ham supporter - and many more silently, one can only imagine - hopes that Bristol City undertake some reciprocation of their own by charging the same prices when the promotion-chasers travel to Ashton Gate on New Year's Day.

#2159. Billy Sharp sends EFL Championship promotion warning to Birmingham City

EFL legend and all-time Championship top scorer Billy Sharp has warned Birmingham City that there's still "a long way to go" after Chris Davies' side reached the second-tier summit ahead of the ongoing international break.

The Blues enjoyed an exceptional run of games between the three-week break in September and October and this current one, winning six of their seven games, three by at least a three-goal margin.

They dropped points only at Cardiff City, a side that has yet to lose at home this season, and have maintained their own unbeaten home record, winning all four games to add some gloss to a St Andrew's record which was pretty draw-heavy in the infancy of the campaign.

The win against former table-toppers Swansea City saw them climb above Middlesbrough on goal difference, and they will hold that top spot for at least another week until action resumes ahead of the Christmas period.

The question in the meantime, though, is: Can they stay there?

Billy Sharp has been a regular pundit on EFL shows this season, after formally announcing his retirement from the professional game back in October. The 40-year-old was promoted out of the Championship three times in his career, so he knows what it takes to maintain top-two form.

The all-time Championship top scorer waxed lyrical over Birmingham through the opening 15 games of the campaign, and was actually surprised that their run to the top of the table hasn't been given as much attention as it arguably should have.

FLW looks at which of the division's 24 clubs are the biggest and lowest spenders

"I think you saw glimpses last season, but they obviously didn't have that consistency," he told the Essential EFL Podcast. "They've done it really quietly, actually; no one's really spoken about them.

"He’s got the two settled centre-halves, which I've liked since last season, and I think he's playing a 4-2-3-1, which really suits him at the minute.

"He seems to have a settled side and had a little sprinkle with Millar coming in, adding a bit of magic down the left, and Stansfield got the two goals, which should do him a world of good. We know he’s got the ability, and when he’s firing, he can win games for Birmingham."

It's so far, so good for the Blues this season, but we are just 15 games in. With over two-thirds of the year still to go, and just one point separating Chris Davies' side from West Brom in fifth, Sharp feels that they can't rest on their laurels at all.

"Am I surprised they're top? I am," he admitted. "But we were saying this about Swansea on the last international break.

"It’s still tight at the top, fair play to Birmingham; going into this international break they are top, but there’s still a long way to go."

As Sharp mentioned, Birmingham's current run of six wins in seven to reach the top of the Championship has gone slightly under the radar, with the main second-tier narratives surrounding West Ham United's drop-off, or Middlesbrough struggling without Will Lankshear, for example.

Now, though, this Blues side are at the forefront of the conversation, and will be until league action resumes after the international break. Chris Davies' side are there to be shot at, and all eyes will be on whether they can handle the weight of expectation.

It's arguable that they didn't last season, with many expecting them to follow in the footsteps of Ipswich Town and make it back-to-back promotions after their record-breaking 111-point campaign in League One the year prior.

#2158. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.
